subtitle: How Kannada Became the Language of Rules and Numbers

panels.shot: dramatic split-wide, half filled with temple town of Shravanabelagola, half with a busy Hoysala market, the two scholars large in the foreground turning toward each side
panels.action: Kesiraja stands robed and composed against the hill and basadi of Shravanabelagola, palm-leaf manuscript in hand, while Rajaditya, with a counting board and stylus, faces a bustling Hoysala marketplace, both sharing the frame like twin flames of Kannada learning.

dialogue.text: In Hoysala Karnataka, Kesiraja shaped Kannada grammar and Rajaditya cast numbers into Kannada words, quietly bending elite knowledge toward the tongue of the land.

i18n.hi: होयसला कर्नाटक में केसिराज ने कन्नड़ का व्याकरण गढ़ा, राजादित्य ने नंबरों को कन्नड़ शब्दों में ढाला—चुपचाप ऊँचे ज्ञान को जमीन की जुबान की तरफ मोड़ दिया।

panels.shot: broad atmospheric wide over Hoysala countryside
panels.action: Rolling hills and fertile fields stretch toward a stone temple-city, with Shravanabelagola’s great hill rising in the distance, while caravans move along dusty roads under a soft morning sky.

dialogue.text: By the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, Hoysala Karnataka was a land of sharp stone and sharper words, where temples rose and poets sang in Kannada beside the old authority of Sanskrit.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं–तेरहवीं सदी तक होयसला कर्नाटक पत्थर की धार और शब्दों की धार वाला देश था—मंदिर उठते थे, कवि कन्नड़ में गाते थे, संस्कृत की पुरानी सत्ता के साथ–साथ।

panels.shot: intimate interior mid-shot inside a Jain or Shaiva matha library
panels.action: In a dim palm-leaf library, Kesiraja and Rajaditya sit at different low desks among monks and scholars, lamplight flickering on stacked manuscripts and hanging charts of syllables and numerals.

dialogue.text: In such halls, learned men still turned first to Sanskrit for rules and reckoning. Yet two Kannada scholars began asking a quiet question: why not in our own tongue?

i18n.hi: ऐसे सभागृहों में विद्वान नियम और हिसाब के लिए पहले संस्कृत की तरफ ही मुड़ते थे। तभी दो कन्नड़ पंडितों ने मन में प्रश्न उभारा: क्यों नहीं हमारी अपनी ज़ुबान में?

panels.shot: slow push-in on Kesiraja-side of the duo, Rajaditya blurred
panels.action: Focus on Kesiraja, middle-aged and steady, tracing syllables on a palm leaf with a stylus, lips moving as he tests sounds; Rajaditya appears behind him, half-shadowed, counting on his fingers over a slate.

dialogue.text: Kesiraja would polish Kannada itself into a mirror of rules. Rajaditya would bend practical arithmetic into Kannada verse. Each worked alone, yet together they shifted the direction of learning.

i18n.hi: केसिराज ने कन्नड़ को ही नियमों का चमकता दर्पण बनाया। राजादित्य ने रोज़मर्रा की गणित को कन्नड़ छंदों में मोड़ा। अलग–अलग काम करते हुए भी, दोनों ने सीखने की दिशा बदल दी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Shravanabelagola hill with Kesiraja in foreground
panels.action: At Shravanabelagola, Kesiraja stands near a basadi, watching pilgrims climb the hill, palm-leaf bundle under his arm, the white stone of the colossal statue towering in the sun beyond.

dialogue.text: Around 1260 CE, in the Jain centre of Shravanabelagola, Kesiraja completed Shabdamanidarpana, the Jewel-Mirror of Grammar, placing Kannada on the examination table of formal grammatical science.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1260 ई. के आसपास, जैन केंद्र श्रवणबेलगोला में केसिराज ने ‘शब्दमणिदर्पण’ पूरा किया—व्याकरण का रत्न–दर्पण—कन्नड़ को औपचारिक व्याकरण–शास्त्र की कसौटी पर रख दिया।

panels.action: We look over Kesiraja’s shoulder at neat lines of Kannada script on palm leaves, small marginal notes beside quoted verses from earlier poets, as his hand hovers thoughtfully above the text.

dialogue.text: He did not invent Kannada. He listened to it. He gathered forms from older works, weighed sounds against Sanskrit models, then set down rules so this living language could stand with a clear spine.

i18n.hi: उसने कन्नड़ रची नहीं, उसे सुना। पुराने ग्रंथों से रूप बटोरे, ध्वनियों को संस्कृत के ढाँचे से तौला, फिर ऐसे नियम गढ़े कि यह जीवित भाषा सीधी रीढ़ के साथ खड़ी हो सके।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Kesiraja before a small assembly of students
panels.action: In a small hall, Kesiraja sits on a low seat explaining with calm intensity, a palm leaf held up; before him, a circle of young scholars repeat syllables and endings, some with Sanskrit texts resting beside Kannada ones.

dialogue.speaker: kesiraja_and_rajaditya
dialogue.text: If Kannada is our speech, should it not also be our subject?

i18n.hi: अगर कन्नड़ हमारी बोलचाल है, तो हमारा विषय भी क्यों न हो?

panels.shot: symbolic side-by-side close-up on two manuscripts
panels.action: Kesiraja’s grammatical manuscript lies beside a Sanskrit grammar text on a mat; in the same frame, Rajaditya’s palm leaf on arithmetic sits next to a Sanskrit arithmetic treatise, both pairs lit by the same lamp.

dialogue.text: This was not rebellion against Sanskrit. Kesiraja drew on its methods. Rajaditya would draw on its mathematics. Their boldness lay in turning those tools toward Kannada as a language of analysis.

i18n.hi: यह संस्कृत के खिलाफ बगावत नहीं थी। केसिराज ने उसकी पद्धति ली, राजादित्य उसकी गणित। साहस इस बात में था कि वही औज़ार अब कन्नड़ पर चले—विश्लेषण की भाषा के रूप में।

panels.action: In a lively Hoysala market, Rajaditya stands near merchants weighing goods and arguing over accounts, observing silently while a trader rolls cowrie shells to tally a deal.

dialogue.text: Somewhere in this world of buying and selling, a Kannada scholar named Rajaditya watched numbers decide fortunes, and carried that concern back to his verses in Vyavaharaganita, Practical Mathematics.

i18n.hi: कहीं इसी व्यापारिक दुनिया में, कन्नड़ पंडित राजादित्य ने देखा कि अंक कैसे किस्मत तय करते हैं, और वह चिंता लेकर ‘व्यवहारगणित’—व्यावहारिक गणित—की अपनी कविताओं में लौट आया।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of Rajaditya composing
panels.action: Rajaditya sits cross-legged, lips moving as he composes, a counting board beside him marked with lines, palm leaves spread out, as he crafts metered Kannada verses about interest, shares and measures.

dialogue.text: His work, likely from the twelfth century, did not chase abstract theory. It spoke of loans, interest, partnership shares and measures, casting commercial arithmetic into Kannada words for trained readers.

i18n.hi: उसकी रचना, शायद बारहवीं सदी की, सूखी सिद्धांत–बहस के पीछे नहीं भागी। उसने कर्ज, ब्याज, हिस्सेदारी और नाप–तौल पर बात की, कारोबार की गणित को कन्नड़ शब्दों में ढालकर पढ़े–लिखों के लिए रखा।

panels.shot: close-up on Rajaditya’s face in thought, numbers faintly superimposed around
panels.action: A close view shows Rajaditya’s brow furrowed, eyes distant, with faint, ghost-like lines of Kannada numerals and metrical feet around him, as if he measures how to fit calculation into verse.

dialogue.speaker: kesiraja_and_rajaditya
dialogue.text: Let the merchant who knows Kannada rhyme his reckoning, not fear it.

i18n.hi: जो व्यापारी कन्नड़ जानता है, वह अपना हिसाब गुनगुनाए, उससे घबराए नहीं।

panels.shot: scholarly interior with Rajaditya and others
panels.action: Rajaditya reads a verse aloud to a handful of scribes and court officials in a lamplit chamber, some nodding as they follow calculations on their own leaves, one quietly compares a Sanskrit text at his side.

dialogue.text: His audience was still elite—scribes, officials, learned traders. Sanskrit treatises remained close at hand. But now, there was a path for arithmetic instruction that ran through the familiar cadence of Kannada.

i18n.hi: उसके श्रोता अभी भी खास थे—कायस्थ, अफसर, पढ़े–लिखे सौदागर। संस्कृत ग्रंथ अभी भी पास रखे जाते थे। पर अब गणित सिखाने की एक राह कन्नड़ की जानी–पहचानी लय से भी होकर जाती थी।

panels.shot: symbolic montage, Kesiraja with letters, Rajaditya with numerals
panels.action: Kesiraja stands amid floating Kannada letters and grammatical terms, while Rajaditya stands opposite amid stylized Kannada numerals and measures, the space between them bridged by a glowing path of text.

dialogue.text: One made Kannada itself an object of rule, quoting older literature to fix its forms. The other made numbers walk through Kannada, shaping verse around real calculations. Words and digits met in the same tongue.

i18n.hi: एक ने कन्नड़ को खुद नियमों का विषय बनाया, पुराने साहित्य के हवाले से उसके रूप तय किए। दूसरे ने अंकों को कन्नड़ में चला कर, असली गणनाओं के इर्द–गिर्द छंद रचे। शब्द और अंक एक ही ज़ुबान में मिले।

panels.shot: library bird’s-eye over stacked palm-leaf bundles
panels.action: From above, bundles of palm leaves are tied and labelled, some containing Shabdamanidarpana, others Vyavaharaganita, mixed among many Sanskrit works in a crowded library of a matha or court.

dialogue.text: Later centuries would quote Kesiraja when discussing Kannada. Rajaditya’s arithmetic survived in manuscript, edited in modern times. Together, they show Kannada stepping into domains once reserved for another script.

i18n.hi: बाद की सदियों में कन्नड़ पर चर्चा करते हुए केसिराज के उद्धरण दिए गए। राजादित्य की गणित पांडुलिपियों में बची रही, आधुनिक समय में संपादित हुई। दोनों मिलकर दिखाते हैं कि कन्नड़ उन क्षेत्रों में दाखिल हुई जो कभी दूसरी लिपि के लिए थे।

panels.shot: soft-focus shot of a modern scholar with old manuscripts
panels.action: A modern researcher in simple dress studies fragile palm leaves of Shabdamanidarpana and Vyavaharaganita under careful light, Shravanabelagola’s hill faintly visible through the window behind.

dialogue.text: Today, historians read these texts not as proof of mass literacy, but as signs that even in elite circles, Kannada was claimed for serious work: grammar, quotation, calculation and instruction.

i18n.hi: आज इतिहासकार इन ग्रंथों को जन–साक्षरता का सबूत नहीं, बल्कि निशानी मानते हैं कि ऊँचे हलकों में भी कन्नड़ को गंभीर काम के लिए माँगा गया—व्याकरण, उद्धरण, गणना और शिक्षा के लिए।

panels.shot: low-angle trio: Kesiraja, Rajaditya, and a generic later Kannada writer
panels.action: Kesiraja and Rajaditya stand in dignified poses, flanked by a later Kannada author holding a printed book, all three framed by carved Hoysala pillars, the sky beyond glowing like a turning page.

dialogue.text: Their choices did not erase Sanskrit science or learning. They added another stream. Through them, Kannada proved it could carry rules and numbers, preparing the way for later scholars to write more in it.

i18n.hi: उनके फैसलों ने संस्कृत की विद्या मिटाई नहीं, उसमें एक और धारा जोड़ दी। इन्हीं के ज़रिए कन्नड़ ने साबित किया कि वह नियम और नंबर संभाल सकती है, आगे के पंडितों के लिए राह साफ कर सकती है।

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up on mirrored surface reflecting Kannada script
panels.action: A polished metal mirror lies on a manuscript, reflecting neat Kannada lines from Shabdamanidarpana and a verse of Vyavaharaganita, while Kesiraja and Rajaditya stand blurred in the background like distant guardians.

dialogue.text: In the Jewel-Mirror of Grammar and in Kannada verses of commerce, we see one enduring truth: knowledge grows roots when it speaks in the language that already lives on people’s tongues.

i18n.hi: व्याकरण के रत्न–दर्पण में और व्यापार की कन्नड़ कविताओं में हम एक स्थायी बात देखते हैं: ज्ञान वहीं जड़ पकड़ता है, जहाँ वह लोगों की जीती–जागती ज़ुबान में बोलता है।

title_i18n.en: The Grammar Mirror and Kannada Numbers
title_i18n.hi: व्याकरण का दर्पण और कन्नड़ की गिनती

subtitle_i18n.en: How Kannada Became the Language of Rules and Numbers
subtitle_i18n.hi: कन्नड़ कैसे बनी नियमों और नंबरों की भाषा
